title: Watchguard / Lockout
shortDescription: Furnace failed to ignite and entered watchguard mode.
fullDescription: One flash on Ducane (Lennox-built) furnace indicates a watchguard lockout. Furnace failed to ignite and will retry after one hour.
safetyWarning: Smell for gas before resetting.

fixSteps.title: Clean sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Polish flame rod with emery cloth.

faq.a: Power off 30 sec or wait 1 hour.

title: Pressure Switch Stuck Closed
fullDescription: Two flashes means switch closed when it should be open. Stuck diaphragm or shorted wire.

title: Pressure Switch Stuck Open
shortDescription: Switch did not close after inducer started.
fullDescription: Three flashes mean inducer ran but switch never closed. Vent block, condensate, or weak inducer.
safetyWarning: Do not run with blocked vent.

title: Limit Switch Open
fullDescription: Four flashes mean high-limit opened. Airflow restriction is the typical cause.
safetyWarning: Repeated trips can damage heat exchanger.

title: Reversed Polarity
fullDescription: Five flashes mean line voltage is wired with reversed polarity.
safetyWarning: Electrical hazard.

title: Flame Without Call
shortDescription: Flame sensed when valve should be off.
fullDescription: Six flashes indicate flame is detected without a heat call. Possible gas valve leak.
safetyWarning: Possible gas leak; close manual valve.

title: Flame Out of Sequence
fullDescription: Seven flashes mean flame appeared earlier than expected in the start sequence. Possible standing flame or gas valve issue.
safetyWarning: Gas valve issue likely.

title: Igniter Circuit Fault
fullDescription: Eight flashes indicate the board sees no current through the igniter during the warm-up period.

title: Low Flame Sense
fullDescription: Nine flashes warn the flame microamp signal is low. Clean the sensor.

title: Gas Valve Output Error
fullDescription: Ten flashes indicate the gas valve output relay is faulted.
safetyWarning: Gas valve issue; call pro.

title: Gas valve relay
fullDescription: Gas valve relay error. Common diagnostic code on Ducane furnace. Resolve by following manufacturer service procedure for the implicated subsystem.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power for 10 minutes, then restore.

fixSteps.title: Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the implicated component, wiring, and connectors.

fixSteps.title: Test/replace
fixSteps.instruction: Test sensor with multimeter or replace if reading abnormal.

fixSteps.title: Verify
fixSteps.instruction: Restore power, clear codes, run system to verify.

safetyWarning: Gas/electric appliance — turn off gas and disconnect electrical power before servicing.
whenToCallPro: Gas-appliance work usually requires licensed HVAC tech.

faq.a: Resolve before continued use to prevent damage or safety hazard.

title: Flame Roll-Out Switch Tripped
shortDescription: A roll-out limit detected flames escaping the burner box and tripped the manual-reset safety switch.
fullDescription: The flame roll-out switch is a manual-reset thermal safety mounted at the front of the burner assembly. When flames or hot gases escape the combustion chamber instead of being drawn into the heat exchanger, the switch trips and de-energizes the gas valve. Common causes include a blocked heat exchanger, weak draft inducer, or cracked heat exchanger.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Weak or failing draft inducer motor
Restricted flue or vent terminal (snow, nest, debris)

symptoms: Furnace will not light and burner area shows soot
Hot smell or scorched paint near the burner box
Manual-reset button on the burner-area switch has popped out
Repeated lockouts on cold days only

fixSteps.title: Shut Off Power and Gas
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the furnace power switch and close the gas shutoff before opening the burner compartment.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Burner Area
fixSteps.instruction: Look for soot, scorched insulation, or melted wires around the burners — these are signs of flame roll-out.

fixSteps.title: Check Vent Terminals
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the exhaust and intake terminals outdoors for blockage. Clear snow, nests, or debris.

fixSteps.title: Reset the Switch
fixSteps.instruction: After confirming no damage and clear vents, press the manual reset button on the roll-out switch firmly until it clicks.

fixSteps.title: Have Heat Exchanger Inspected
fixSteps.instruction: If the switch trips again, stop using the furnace and have a licensed technician perform a heat-exchanger integrity inspection.

whenToCallPro: If the switch trips a second time, the heat exchanger is suspect — call a licensed technician immediately. A cracked exchanger is a carbon-monoxide hazard.

faq.q: Can I keep running the furnace with this code?
faq.a: If the furnace still produces heat, you can run it short-term, but address the issue promptly because related safety circuits may shut it down without warning.

faq.q: Will resetting the furnace clear this?
faq.a: A power-cycle reset may clear a temporary fault, but if the underlying condition (sensor, motor, valve, vent) is still present the code will return on the next call for heat.

title: High-Limit Switch Open — Overheat Condition
shortDescription: The plenum high-limit switch opened due to excessive supply-air temperature.
fullDescription: The high-limit switch is a normally-closed thermal safety in the supply plenum. When supply-air temperature climbs above the rated limit (typically 160-200°F), the switch opens to shut off the gas valve and prevent damage to the heat exchanger. The blower continues running to dissipate heat. Repeated trips usually mean restricted airflow rather than a faulty switch.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Dirty or clogged air filter restricting return airflow
Closed or blocked supply registers / undersized return duct
Failed or slow blower motor (bad capacitor, bearings)
Incorrect blower speed tap for installed system

symptoms: Burners light then shut off after 1-3 minutes while blower keeps running
Supply registers feel very hot then very cool

fixSteps.title: Replace the Air Filter
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the filter and check for restriction. Replace any filter older than 60 days or visibly grey.

fixSteps.title: Open All Supply Registers
fixSteps.instruction: Walk the home and confirm every supply register is fully open and unobstructed by furniture or rugs.

fixSteps.title: Verify Return-Air Path
fixSteps.instruction: Check that return grilles are not blocked and that the blower-compartment door is fully sealed.

fixSteps.title: Measure Temperature Rise
fixSteps.instruction: With a thermometer, measure return and supply temperatures during a heat call. Compare against the data plate's listed rise (typically 30-60°F).

fixSteps.title: Test Blower and Capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: If temperature rise is too high, test the run capacitor and inspect the blower wheel for buildup. Replace components as needed.

whenToCallPro: If airflow is unrestricted but the limit still trips, call a technician to verify gas input pressure and check for a failing blower or undersized ductwork.

title: ECM Blower Motor Communication Fault
shortDescription: The control board has lost communication with the variable-speed ECM blower motor.
fullDescription: Modern furnaces use ECM (Electronically Commutated Motor) blowers that communicate with the control board over a low-voltage signal harness. When the board cannot read motor RPM feedback or the motor's onboard module fails to acknowledge speed commands, the system flags an ECM communication fault and falls back to either off or a fixed safety speed.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Loose or corroded ECM motor harness connector
Failed ECM motor control module (back of motor)
Control board ECM driver section failed
Voltage spike from recent storm or power event

symptoms: Blower will not run on heat or cool calls
Blower runs at one fixed speed regardless of mode
Audible chirping or single-rotation pulse from motor
Diagnostic code on board indicates motor / ECM fault

fixSteps.title: Cycle Power for 60 Seconds
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the furnace breaker for one full minute to allow the ECM module to fully discharge and reinitialize.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Motor Harness
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, unplug and reseat both the 5-pin power and 16-pin control connectors at the motor. Look for burned pins or moisture.

fixSteps.title: Check Capacitor (PSC fallback models)
fixSteps.instruction: On hybrid models with a run capacitor, test it for proper microfarad rating.

fixSteps.title: Test for 120/240V at Motor
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm correct line voltage at the motor's power plug during a call for blower.

fixSteps.title: Replace Motor or Module
fixSteps.instruction: If line voltage is present and signals are correct but the motor is silent, the ECM module or motor must be replaced.

whenToCallPro: If reseating connectors does not restore communication, ECM motors must be matched to the model and replaced by a qualified technician.

title: Condensate Overflow Switch Open
shortDescription: A float or overflow switch detected high water in the condensate pan or drain trap.
fullDescription: High-efficiency (90%+) furnaces produce condensate that must drain freely. A float switch in the secondary drain pan or inline trap will open and shut down the furnace if water backs up. Common causes are a clogged condensate trap, blocked drain line, frozen drain in winter, or a failed condensate pump.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Clogged condensate trap with biological slime
Blocked or kinked drain hose to floor drain or pump
Failed condensate pump (motor or check valve)

symptoms: Furnace will not start; water visible in secondary pan or under unit
Pressure-switch or limit faults that clear after pumping out water
Condensate pump hums but does not move water

fixSteps.title: Pump Out Standing Water
fixSteps.instruction: Use a wet/dry vac to remove water from the secondary pan and the drain trap inlet.

fixSteps.title: Clean the Condensate Trap
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the trap, flush with warm water and a small amount of distilled vinegar, then reinstall.

fixSteps.title: Clear Drain Line
fixSteps.instruction: Run a thin brush or shop vac through the entire drain line to the termination point.

fixSteps.title: Test Condensate Pump
fixSteps.instruction: Pour water directly into the pump reservoir; the pump should activate and discharge water within seconds.

fixSteps.title: Verify Float Switch
fixSteps.instruction: With trap clear, jumper the float switch terminals briefly to confirm operation, then restore wiring.

whenToCallPro: If the drain repeatedly clogs, a technician can re-pitch the trap, add a cleanout, or upsize the line. Frozen exterior runs may require heat tape or a redesign.

title: Line-Voltage Polarity Reversed or Open Ground
shortDescription: Control board detected reversed hot/neutral or a missing equipment ground.
fullDescription: The control board uses the chassis ground as a reference for flame-rectification sensing. If line voltage is wired with hot and neutral reversed, or if the equipment ground is open, the flame signal cannot be read reliably and the board flags a polarity / ground fault before allowing ignition.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Hot and neutral reversed at outlet, disconnect, or whip
Loose neutral at panel or junction box
Use of an ungrounded extension cord (temporary install)
Failed surge protector creating impedance on neutral

symptoms: Furnace will not progress past initial diagnostic
Code clears momentarily then returns when neighbor's appliance starts
Faint shock when touching cabinet (open ground)
Flame proves intermittently and drops out

fixSteps.title: Verify Power at Service Switch
fixSteps.instruction: With a multimeter on the line side of the furnace switch, confirm 120V hot-to-neutral, 120V hot-to-ground, and 0V neutral-to-ground.

fixSteps.title: Test Receptacle Polarity
fixSteps.instruction: If the furnace is cord-connected, plug a 3-light receptacle tester into the outlet to verify wiring.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Ground Wire
fixSteps.instruction: Open the furnace junction box and confirm the bare or green ground wire is firmly attached to the chassis ground screw.

fixSteps.title: Correct Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: If polarity is reversed at the outlet or disconnect, shut off the breaker and swap the hot and neutral conductors at the device.

fixSteps.title: Power Up and Retest
fixSteps.instruction: Restore power and verify the code clears and ignition completes normally.

whenToCallPro: If your service feed itself shows reversed polarity or a floating neutral, contact your utility or a licensed electrician — do not work inside the panel.

title: Communicating Bus Fault Between Thermostat and Furnace
shortDescription: The communicating thermostat cannot reliably exchange data with the furnace control.
fullDescription: Communicating systems use a 2-wire data bus (often labeled 1/2 or A/B) to exchange staging, fan, and diagnostic data between the thermostat, indoor unit, and outdoor unit. Wiring errors, polarity reversal on the data pair, or interference from a thermostat 'C-wire' adapter can break communication and force the system to a non-communicating fallback or full lockout.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Data wires reversed at thermostat or furnace terminal
Long wire run with too small a gauge causing voltage drop
Thermostat firmware mismatched with control board
Failed thermostat or control board communication chip
Damaged thermostat cable (staple through, rodent damage)

symptoms: Thermostat displays 'communication error', 'No comm', or blank screen
Furnace runs only on emergency / non-communicating mode
Outdoor unit will not stage up despite cold temperatures
Intermittent operation that improves after a power cycle

fixSteps.title: Power-Cycle Both Ends
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the furnace breaker AND remove the thermostat from its base for 60 seconds, then reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Verify Wire Landings
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the data pair lands on the matching terminals at both the thermostat and the furnace control.

fixSteps.title: Check for Damaged Cable
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the thermostat cable along its run for staples, kinks, or chew marks. Replace any damaged section.

fixSteps.title: Update or Match Firmware
fixSteps.instruction: If the brand offers a firmware update via the thermostat menu or app, run it. Otherwise verify model compatibility.

fixSteps.title: Substitute Thermostat
fixSteps.instruction: If a known-good thermostat communicates correctly, the original thermostat is at fault.

whenToCallPro: If wiring is correct and both thermostat and board are confirmed compatible, the comm chip on the control board may be failed and require replacement.

title: Draft Inducer Locked Rotor or Out-of-Range Current
shortDescription: The control measured inducer current outside the expected range, indicating a stalled or shorted motor.
fullDescription: The control board monitors current draw on the draft inducer. When current is too low (open winding, broken connection) or too high (locked rotor, shorted winding, debris jamming the wheel), the board aborts the heat call and flags an inducer-fault code. Continuing to run a stalled motor can melt the housing or trip the breaker.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Inducer wheel obstructed by debris (insulation, leaves)
Loose motor wiring at control board

symptoms: Inducer hums but does not spin, or spins very slowly
Breaker trips when furnace calls for heat
Smell of hot motor windings near the inducer
Pressure switch never closes because draft is too weak

fixSteps.title: Cut Power Immediately
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off the furnace switch to prevent further damage to the stalled motor.

fixSteps.title: Check for Obstruction
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, remove the inducer cover and verify the wheel spins freely by hand.

fixSteps.title: Test the Run Capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: If the inducer uses a capacitor, measure microfarads. Replace if more than 10% out of spec.

fixSteps.title: Measure Motor Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: With leads disconnected, ohm out the motor windings; an open or near-zero reading means the motor is bad.

fixSteps.title: Replace Inducer Assembly
fixSteps.instruction: If the motor is seized or burned, replace the entire inducer assembly with the OEM part for that model.

whenToCallPro: A burned-smelling motor or repeatedly tripping breaker requires professional replacement to avoid fire risk.

title: Twinning Wire / Phase Mismatch Between Paired Units
shortDescription: Two furnaces wired to share a single thermostat are out of phase or twinning wire is open.
fullDescription: Some homes use two furnaces ducted into a common plenum and 'twinned' so they fire together. The twinning wire synchronizes the two control boards so blowers and ignition run simultaneously. If line-voltage phasing is mismatched between the two units or the twinning conductor opens, one or both units will lock out with a twinning fault.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Twinning wire broken, disconnected, or wrong terminal
Two units fed from opposite legs of 240V split-phase service
Different control board firmware between paired units
Only one of two breakers tripped or off

symptoms: One furnace runs and the other does not, despite both calling
Both units fault simultaneously on heat call
Diagnostic LED indicates twinning or phase fault
Erratic blower behavior — one blower starts, the other coasts

fixSteps.title: Verify Both Breakers On
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm both furnace breakers are fully on and the service switches are closed.

fixSteps.title: Check Twinning Wire
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the dedicated twinning conductor between the two control boards for proper landing and continuity.

fixSteps.title: Confirm Phase Match
fixSteps.instruction: At each furnace, measure hot-to-ground; both should read the same nominal voltage from the same leg of the panel.

fixSteps.title: Equalize Firmware
fixSteps.instruction: If the boards are different revisions, contact the manufacturer for matched-firmware replacements.

fixSteps.title: Test Twinned Operation
fixSteps.instruction: After repairs, force a heat call and confirm both units ignite, run, and shut down together.

whenToCallPro: Correcting service-leg phasing requires opening the panel and should be done by a licensed electrician.

title: Two-Stage Gas Valve Failure to Switch Stages
shortDescription: The control board commanded high-fire but the gas valve stayed on low-fire, or vice versa.
fullDescription: Two-stage and modulating gas valves use one or more low-voltage solenoids to switch between firing rates. The control board monitors flame current and stage-feedback to confirm the valve responded. If the valve fails to switch within the timing window, the system either runs single-stage as a fallback or locks out depending on how many calls fail.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Failed second-stage solenoid coil in the valve
Loose or corroded HI/LO wires at the gas valve
Control board not outputting 24V on stage-2 terminal
Gas pressure too low to support high-fire

symptoms: Furnace appears to run continuously without reaching setpoint
Flame size visibly does not change between stages
Long heat cycles in cold weather despite proper sizing
Stage-1 only operation indicated on diagnostic readout

fixSteps.title: Reset Control Board
fixSteps.instruction: Power-cycle the furnace and observe the next heat call to see whether stage-2 attempts to engage.

fixSteps.title: Verify Stage Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the HI and LO conductors are landed on the correct terminals at both the valve and the board.

fixSteps.title: Measure 24V at Stage-2
fixSteps.instruction: During a stage-2 call, measure 24V across the HI solenoid terminals; absence of voltage means the board is at fault.

fixSteps.title: Test Manifold Pressure
fixSteps.instruction: A technician should manometer the manifold on both stages and compare to the rating plate.

fixSteps.title: Replace the Gas Valve
fixSteps.instruction: If 24V is present but the stage does not change and pressure is correct upstream, replace the gas valve.

whenToCallPro: Any gas valve replacement or manometer test must be done by a licensed gas technician — leak testing is mandatory after reassembly.

faq.q: Can I keep running the furnace with this code?
faq.a: If the furnace still produces heat, you can run it short-term, but address the issue promptly because related safety circuits may shut it down without warning.

faq.q: Will resetting the furnace clear this?
faq.a: A power-cycle reset may clear a temporary fault, but if the underlying condition (sensor, motor, valve, vent) is still present the code will return on the next call for heat.

title: Outdoor / Supply Thermistor Out of Range
shortDescription: A temperature sensor used by the furnace is reading outside its valid range, blocking proper staging.
fullDescription: Modern furnaces use NTC thermistors on the supply plenum and (on heat-pump systems) on the outdoor coil to optimize staging, blower speed, and dual-fuel switchover. When a thermistor reads as a short (~0Ω) or open (∞Ω), the board cannot calculate temperature and either reverts to default behavior or shuts down depending on which sensor failed.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Sensor wire pinched in cabinet or chewed by rodents
Sensor dislodged from clip or well
Wrong sensor type installed (different resistance curve)

symptoms: Furnace runs but blower stays on lowest speed regardless of demand
Dual-fuel system never crosses over to gas heat below balance point
Diagnostic readout shows -40°F or 200°F when ambient is moderate
Sensor-fault icon on the thermostat or control display

fixSteps.title: Locate the Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Refer to the wiring diagram on the blower door to find the affected thermistor.

fixSteps.title: Inspect and Reseat
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the sensor, examine the pins for green corrosion, and reseat firmly into the connector.

fixSteps.title: Measure Resistance at Room Temp
fixSteps.instruction: With sensor disconnected from the board, measure resistance and compare against the model's resistance-vs-temperature chart.

fixSteps.title: Replace the Thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Install an OEM replacement of the matching type and reconnect the harness.

fixSteps.title: Verify Reading on Diagnostic Display
fixSteps.instruction: Power up and confirm the reported temperature on the board's readout matches the actual ambient.

whenToCallPro: If multiple sensors read out of range simultaneously, the control board's analog input is suspect and should be tested by a technician.

faq.q: Can I keep running the furnace with this code?
faq.a: If the furnace still produces heat, you can run it short-term, but address the issue promptly because related safety circuits may shut it down without warning.

faq.q: Will resetting the furnace clear this?
faq.a: A power-cycle reset may clear a temporary fault, but if the underlying condition (sensor, motor, valve, vent) is still present the code will return on the next call for heat.
